note.text:
We use the Past Perfect for an action that happened before another action in the past.
Form: had + the past participle, the same for every person: I had finished, she had left, they had eaten.
“When the ambulance arrived, the nurse had already stopped the bleeding.” (First the nurse stopped the bleeding; then the ambulance arrived.)
Signal words: already, before, after, by the time, when.
Negative: hadn't + participle: “We hadn't eaten.” Question: “Had you finished?” — “Yes, I had.”
The later action is in the Simple Past: “By the time we got there, the meeting had begun.”

worked_example.problem: Join the two actions in one sentence: First the nurse {past(v)} {c}. Then {a}.
steps: The earlier action goes in the Past Perfect: had + {participle(v)}.
The later action stays in the Simple Past: {a}.

cards.idea: The Past Perfect is had + the past participle, for every person.
The Past Perfect shows which past action came first.
example: When we arrived, the film had started. (The film started first.)
When we arrived, the film started. (We arrived first.)

cards.idea: By the time, already and before often go with the Past Perfect.
example: By the time the lorries came, the families had left.
She had already eaten before the visitors arrived.

pick.s: By the time we reached the hospital, the baby ___ born.
e: It is a past story: had been.
It is a past story: had been.

pick.s: She ___ already cooked when her husband came home.
e: Earlier past action: had.
Earlier past action: had.

pick.s: The volunteers had left ___ the rain started.
e: Before shows which came first.
For goes with a length of time.

pick.s: When the fire brigade arrived, the fire ___ the roof.
e: Earlier past action: had destroyed.
It is a past story.

pick.a: the relief lorries reached the village

questions.prompt: Write the verb in the Past Perfect.

misconceptions.explain: This action came first: had + the past participle, had {participle(X.v)}.
After had, use the past participle: {participle(X.v)}.
It is in the past: had, not have.

pick.q: When I got to the stop, the bus had left.
e: had left is the earlier action.
had left shows the bus left earlier.
Both actions happened.
pick.y: The Past Perfect (had left) is the earlier action.

pick.q: The volunteers had cleaned the hall before the guests arrived.
e: had cleaned is the earlier action.
before shows an order.
The volunteers cleaned it.

pick.q: By the time the doctor came, the nurse had given first aid.
e: had given is the earlier action.
By the time shows an order.
The nurse gave it.

pick.q: We had eaten when Dad came home.
e: had eaten is the earlier action.
had eaten shows we ate first.
We ate.

pick.a: The bus had left when we arrived.
pick.b: The bus had left when we arrived.

pick.a: She had already eaten before the visitors came.
pick.b: She had already eaten before the visitors came.

pick.a: By the time help came, the fire had spread.
pick.b: By the time help came, the fire had spread.

pick.a: We hadn't seen the flood before.
pick.b: We hadn't seen the flood before.

questions.prompt: Tap the words in the right order.
One sentence has a mistake. Which one?

right.text: When we arrived, the film had started.
By the time help came, the river had flooded the road.

wrong.text: When we arrived, the meeting had began.
wrong.explain: The participle of begin is begun: had begun.

wrong.text: They has finished before we came.
wrong.explain: The Past Perfect uses had for every person: They had finished.
